title: CUET Mass Media Test 1
subject: Mass Media / Mass Communication (Code: 318)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Mass Media - 318.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) Mass Media papers 2024, 2025 and 2026, analysed for format only (no questions copied)
textbooks: CBSE Mass Media Studies, Classes XI-XII (curriculum mirrored by the NTA syllabus)
Constitution of India, Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(2); Acts and Supreme Court judgments as cited
Official histories of All India Radio, Doordarshan and Indian cinema
instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a case; the set stays together.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about public relations:
(A) Ivy Lee is often called the father of modern public relations.
(B) A press release is a written statement issued to the media.
(C) Public relations works only through paid advertising space.
(D) A house journal is a tool for communicating with employees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Ivy Lee set out modern PR principles, a press release informs the media, and a house journal serves employees.
Why not the others: (C) is false. PR mainly earns media coverage rather than buying space. Options (C) and (D) include (C).
Key point: PR builds goodwill with the media, employees and the public.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Marshall McLuhan described a world linked by electronic media as a ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Global village
Why: McLuhan argued that electronic media shrink distances and make the world a global village.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are other terms. (D) is Habermas's idea of a space for public debate.
Key point: McLuhan also said that "the medium is the message".

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of a public relations programme, according to the RACE model, in the correct order:
(A) Communication
(B) Research
(C) Evaluation
(D) Action (planning)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: RACE stands for Research, Action (planning), Communication and Evaluation, in that order.
Why not the others: (A) puts communication before planning. (B) plans before research. (C) evaluates before communicating.
Key point: The RACE model was set out by John Marston.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question: Which is the national helpline number for reporting cyber fraud in India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 1930
Why: 1930 is the national cyber crime helpline, and complaints can also be filed at cybercrime.gov.in.
Why not the others: (B) is Childline. (C) is the emergency response number. (D) is the ambulance service.
Key point: Quick reporting can help freeze money lost to fraud.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question: Media convergence means:
options: A) Merging all the newspapers into one large media company
B) Government taking control of all the media in a country
C) Text, audio and video coming together on one platform
D) Replacing printed newspapers entirely with radio
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Text, audio and video coming together on one platform
Why: Convergence is the coming together of different media forms and technologies on a single digital platform, such as a smartphone.
Why not the others: (A) is ownership concentration. (B) is state control. (D) is not convergence.
Key point: A phone is now newspaper, radio and TV in one.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
(A) The Vernacular Press Act
(B) Press censorship during the Emergency
(C) Hicky's Bengal Gazette
(D) Udant Martand, the first Hindi newspaper
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: Hicky's Bengal Gazette came out in 1780, and Udant Martand in 1826. The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878, and censorship was imposed during the Emergency in 1975.
Why not the others: (A) puts the 1878 Act before 1826. (C) puts Udant Martand before Hicky's paper. (D) puts 1975 before 1878.
Key point: The Indian press grew alongside the freedom struggle.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: A microphone that hears all around
questions.question: A microphone that picks up sound equally from all directions is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Omnidirectional
Why: An omnidirectional microphone picks up sound from every direction equally.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) pick up mainly from the front. (C) picks up from the front and back.
Key point: The pick-up pattern decides where a microphone is used.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question: A film built around chases, fights and stunts belongs to which genre?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Action
Why: Action films rely on physical conflict, chases and stunts.
Why not the others: (B) centres on love. (C) uses songs and dance. (D) recreates the past.
Key point: Genres help audiences know what to expect.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question: Which of the following ethical lapses is wrongly described?
options: A) Plagiarism: passing off another's work as one's own
B) Advertorial: an advertisement made to look like news
C) Sensationalism: reporting only verified official facts
D) Paid news: coverage given in return for money
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Sensationalism: reporting only verified official facts
Why: (C) is wrongly described. Sensationalism means exaggerating or dramatising news to excite the audience.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are correctly described.
Key point: Sensationalism trades accuracy for attention.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Which body, set up in 1997, runs All India Radio and Doordarshan?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Prasar Bharati
Why: Prasar Bharati is India's public service broadcaster, and runs AIR (Akashvani) and Doordarshan.
Why not the others: (A) oversees press ethics. (B) is the government's information agency. (D) measures TV audiences.
Key point: Prasar Bharati was created to give public broadcasting more autonomy.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question:
Arrange the following films in order of their release:
(A) Alam Ara
(B) Manthan
(C) Raja Harishchandra
(D) Pather Panchali
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (C), (A), (D), (B)
Why: Raja Harishchandra came out in 1913 and Alam Ara, the first Indian talkie, in 1931. Pather Panchali followed in 1955 and Manthan in 1976.
Why not the others: (B) puts Alam Ara before 1913. (C) puts Pather Panchali before Alam Ara. (D) puts Manthan before Pather Panchali.
Key point: Silent films gave way to talkies in 1931.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (News value)
(A) Timeliness
(B) Proximity
(C) Prominence
(D) Human interest

List-II (Meaning)
(I) The event happened near the readers
(II) The story touches readers' emotions
(III) The event has just happened
(IV) Well-known people are involved
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Timeliness means the event is recent (III), and proximity means it is near the reader (I). Prominence means well-known people are involved (IV), and human interest touches the emotions (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps timeliness and proximity. (C) swaps proximity and prominence. (D) swaps prominence and human interest.
Key point: News values help editors decide what is newsworthy.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.sub_topic: How the internet changed mass media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about mass media before and after the internet:
(A) Traditional mass media followed a model of a few senders and a vast number of receivers.
(B) Traditional media needed gigantic organisations and a huge technical infrastructure.
(C) On the internet, an individual can post information for a global audience.
(D) The internet has reduced the number of sources for the same information.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D)
Why: (D) is not correct. The internet offers many sources for the same information.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (C) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: The internet broke the few-to-many model.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT good netiquette?
options: A) Identifying yourself clearly in a work email
B) Sending one promotion to hundreds of strangers
C) Asking before sharing someone else's photo
D) Using polite and suitable language in posts
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Sending one promotion to hundreds of strangers
Why: Sending unwanted bulk messages is spam, which netiquette says to avoid.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are good netiquette: identify yourself, respect privacy, use suitable language.
Key point: Netiquette is the etiquette of behaving well online.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question: Which body is the self-regulatory organisation for the content of advertisements in India?
options: A) Advertising Standards Council of India
C) Central Board of Film Certification
D) Telecom Regulatory Authority of India
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Advertising Standards Council of India
Why: The Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI, 1985) handles complaints about misleading or offensive ads.
Why not the others: (B) is the government's media agency. (C) certifies films. (D) regulates telecom.
Key point: ASCI's code asks ads to be honest, decent and fair.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: The red light outside a studio
questions.question: A red "On Air" light glowing outside a radio studio tells people that:
options: A) All the equipment has been switched off
B) A broadcast or recording is in progress
C) The studio is free and ready for cleaning
D) The transmitter has failed and is off air
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A broadcast or recording is in progress
Why: The light warns people not to enter or make noise, because the microphones are live.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not what the light means.
Key point: Studios are soundproofed and their entry is controlled.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: Order of tasks in making a programme
questions.question:
Arrange the following tasks in the order in which they are done while making a television programme:
(A) Editing and dubbing
(B) Writing the script
(C) Shooting on location
(D) A recce of possible locations
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (B), (D), (C), (A)
Why: The script is written first, and a recce of locations follows in pre-production. Shooting is production, and editing and dubbing are post-production.
Why not the others: (A) shoots before the recce. (B) does the recce before there is a script. (D) edits before shooting.
Key point: The three stages are pre-production, production and post-production.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Type of advertising)
(A) Cross promotion
(B) Merchandising
(C) Covert advertising
(D) Public service advertising

List-II (Description)
(I) A message for social good, such as road safety
(II) A product shown within a film or show without being announced as an advertisement
(III) Selling goods such as toys and T-shirts that carry a film's characters or a brand
(IV) Two brands promote each other, such as a film and a soft drink
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: In cross promotion two brands promote each other (IV). Merchandising sells goods carrying a brand or characters (III). Covert advertising places a product inside content (II), and public service ads carry social messages (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps merchandising and covert advertising. (B) swaps cross promotion and merchandising. (D) swaps covert and public service advertising.
Key point: Covert advertising is also called product placement.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question: In documentary making, research before the shoot mainly helps the filmmaker to:
options: A) Hire famous actors for the lead roles
B) Write songs for the soundtrack
C) Find the facts, people and places to film
D) Design sets in a studio
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Find the facts, people and places to film
Why: A documentary records real people and events, so research finds the facts, subjects and locations first.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) belong to fiction films.
Key point: Documentaries deal with reality, not invented stories.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: What the Amul girl ads are known for
questions.question: The Amul girl campaign, running since 1966, is best known for:
options: A) Comparing Amul with rival brands
B) Using film stars in every ad
D) Witty comments on current events
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Witty comments on current events
Why: The Amul ads are topical. They comment on news and events with puns and humour.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) do not describe the campaign.
Key point: A long-running campaign builds a strong brand image.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Models of communication and their thinkers
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Model)
(A) Lasswell
(B) Shannon and Weaver
(C) Osgood and Schramm
(D) Berlo

List-II (Key feature)
(I) A circular model in which both parties encode and decode
(II) "Who says what, in which channel, to whom, with what effect"
(III) Source, Message, Channel, Receiver (SMCR)
(IV) A mathematical model that introduced the idea of noise
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: Lasswell's verbal model asks who says what in which channel to whom with what effect (II). Shannon and Weaver added noise (IV). Osgood and Schramm drew a circular model (I), and Berlo's model is SMCR (III).
Why not the others: (B) swaps Lasswell and Shannon–Weaver. (C) swaps Shannon–Weaver and Osgood–Schramm. (D) swaps Osgood–Schramm and Berlo.
Key point: Linear models came first, and circular models added feedback.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Which element, missing from Lasswell's original model, was stressed by later circular models of communication?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Feedback
Why: Lasswell's model is one-way. Circular models show the receiver responding, which is feedback.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are already part of Lasswell's model.
Key point: Feedback makes communication a two-way process.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question: What does "creating imagery" in a radio script mean?
options: A) Showing photographs of the show on the station's website
B) Packing the script with as many statistics as possible
C) Helping listeners picture scenes through words and sound
D) Describing the studio equipment in detail to listeners
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Helping listeners picture scenes through words and sound
Why: Radio has no pictures, so words, sound effects and music help listeners imagine the scene. This is why radio is called the theatre of the mind.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not what imagery means.
Key point: Good radio writing appeals to the imagination.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.sub_topic: What WordPress and Blogger are for
questions.question: Platforms such as WordPress and Blogger are mainly used for:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Blogging
Why: WordPress and Blogger let users publish blogs, which are regular written posts.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are served by other kinds of platforms.
Key point: Blogging, networking and photo and video sharing are the main types of social media.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question: In the AIDA model of advertising, the letters stand for Attention, Interest, Desire and ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Action
Why: AIDA stands for Attention, Interest, Desire and Action. The ad aims to lead the viewer to act, for example to buy.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not part of the model.
Key point: AIDA describes the steps an ad takes a consumer through.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Krishi Darshan, which Doordarshan began in 1967, was meant mainly for:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Farmers
Why: Krishi Darshan gave farmers information on better farming methods, an early use of TV for development.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) were not its target audience.
Key point: Development communication uses media to bring about social change.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about social media in a democracy:
(A) Citizens can question leaders and institutions directly.
(B) Misinformation can spread very quickly.
(C) Hashtag campaigns can build a collective identity among strangers.
(D) Only governments are allowed to start campaigns on social media.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Social media gives citizens a voice and helps people unite around causes, but it also spreads falsehoods fast.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Anyone can start a campaign, which is the basis of cyber activism. Options (B) and (D) include (D).
Key point: Social media both strengthens and tests democracy.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question: Which principle matters most for a PRO handling a crisis?
options: A) Say nothing until the crisis passes
B) Speak early, accurately and with one voice
C) Deny every report in the media
D) Speak only through paid advertisements
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Speak early, accurately and with one voice
Why: In a crisis, the organisation should give quick, accurate information through one official spokesperson.
Why not the others: (A) lets rumours spread. (C) destroys credibility if the reports are true. (D) looks evasive.
Key point: Trust is the main asset at risk in a crisis.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Scheduling strategy)
(A) Stripping
(B) Stacking
(C) Hammocking
(D) Tent-poling

List-II (Meaning)
(I) Placing similar programmes back to back in a block
(II) Airing a programme at the same time every weekday
(III) Placing a strong programme between two weaker ones
(IV) Placing a new or weak programme between two strong ones
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: Stripping airs a show in the same weekday slot (II), and stacking groups similar shows (I). Hammocking places a weak show between strong ones (IV), and tent-poling places a strong show between weaker ones (III).
Why not the others: (B) swaps stripping and stacking. (C) swaps stacking and hammocking. (D) swaps hammocking and tent-poling.
Key point: Scheduling is used to hold and build audiences.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Pioneer)
(A) Lumière brothers
(B) Robert Flaherty
(C) John Grierson
(D) Dadasaheb Phalke

List-II (Contribution)
(I) Made Nanook of the North
(II) Coined the term "documentary"
(III) Made Raja Harishchandra
(IV) Held the first paid public film show in Paris
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: The Lumière brothers held the first paid public show in Paris in 1895 (IV). Flaherty made Nanook of the North (I). Grierson coined "documentary" (II), and Phalke made Raja Harishchandra (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Flaherty and Grierson. (B) swaps the Lumières and Flaherty. (C) swaps Grierson and Phalke.
Key point: Grierson used the word while reviewing Flaherty's Moana in 1926.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question: A series of drawings showing each planned shot of a programme in order is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Storyboard
Why: A storyboard shows each shot as a drawing, like a comic strip, before shooting begins.
Why not the others: (A) is the written script with camera directions. (B) tells the crew when to report. (C) is the running order of a live show.
Key point: Storyboards save time and money on the set.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Film genres and what defines them
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about film genres:
(A) A genre is the budget category into which a film falls.
(B) Westerns are usually set on the American frontier.
(C) In a musical, songs and dance carry much of the story.
(D) Animation creates movement from drawings, models or computer images shown frame by frame.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (C) and (D) only
Why: (B), (C) and (D) are correct descriptions of the western, the musical and animation.
Why not the others: (A) is false. A genre is a category of films that share conventions of story, setting and style. Options (A), (C) and (D) include (A).
Key point: Genre theory studies these shared conventions.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Early landmarks of television in India
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about television in India:
(A) Television broadcasting began in Delhi in 1959.
(B) The Satellite Instructional Television Experiment (1975–76) beamed programmes to villages.
(C) Colour transmission began in 1982, the year Delhi hosted the Asian Games.
(D) Hum Log, Doordarshan's first soap opera, was a retelling of the Ramayana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. TV began in Delhi on 15 September 1959, SITE used a satellite to reach villages in 1975–76, and colour came in 1982.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Hum Log (1984) was a social serial about a middle-class family. The Ramayan serial came later. Options (B) and (D) include (D).
Key point: Television in India began as a tool for education and development.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question: Ordinary people recording and sharing news events on their phones is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Citizen journalism
Why: Citizen journalism is news gathered and shared by members of the public rather than by professionals.
Why not the others: (A) is sensational reporting. (B) is in-depth digging by professionals. (C) is reporting from within military units.
Key point: The internet lets individuals publish directly.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question: A newspaper report goes viral on social media and is then debated on TV news. This shows how, in the new media age, ____.
options: A) One medium triggers activity in others
B) Each medium works in complete isolation
C) Television has fully replaced print
D) Only print can set the public agenda
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) One medium triggers activity in others
Why: Information in one medium now sets off activity in others, from print to social media to TV.
Why not the others: (B) is the opposite. (C) and (D) are not shown by the example.
Key point: Media today are interlinked.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Equipment)
(A) Dynamic microphone
(B) Condenser microphone
(C) Sound mixer
(D) Amplifier

List-II (Feature)
(I) Strengthens a weak audio signal
(II) Combines and balances several audio inputs
(III) Rugged and needs no power, so it suits outdoor work
(IV) Very sensitive and needs power, often phantom power
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: A dynamic mic is rugged and needs no power (III). A condenser mic is sensitive and needs power (IV). A mixer combines inputs (II), and an amplifier strengthens a signal (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the two microphones. (C) swaps the condenser mic and the mixer. (D) swaps the mixer and the amplifier.
Key point: Choosing the right microphone depends on the setting.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Cyber crime)
(A) Trolling
(B) Cyberstalking
(C) Phishing
(D) Identity theft

List-II (Description)
(I) Posting provocative remarks to upset people
(II) Using someone's personal data to pose as them
(III) Repeatedly tracking and harassing a person online
(IV) Sending fake messages to steal passwords or bank details
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Trolling provokes people (I), and cyberstalking is repeated tracking and harassment (III). Phishing uses fake messages to steal details (IV), and identity theft is posing as someone else (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps trolling and stalking. (B) swaps stalking and phishing. (D) swaps phishing and identity theft.
Key point: Victims can report cyber crime at cybercrime.gov.in.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: When graphics and music are added
questions.question: Graphics, music and colour correction are added to a programme at the ____ stage.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Post-production
Why: These are finishing tasks done after shooting, in post-production.
Why not the others: (B) is planning. (C) is shooting. (D) is delivering the finished programme.
Key point: Editing is the heart of post-production.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: Why radio writers prefer the active voice
questions.question: Why do radio scriptwriters prefer the active voice?
options: A) It is direct and easy to follow by ear
B) It makes sentences longer and richer
C) It sounds more formal and official
D) It lets the writer use technical terms
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) It is direct and easy to follow by ear
Why: Listeners cannot reread a sentence. The active voice is direct and clear at one hearing.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) are the opposite of what radio needs. (D) is wrong, since jargon is avoided on radio.
Key point: Radio is written for the ear, not the eye.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about media law in India:
(A) Freedom of the press is part of the freedom of speech and expression in Article 19(1)(a).
(B) Article 19(2) allows reasonable restrictions, for example on grounds of defamation and contempt of court.
(C) The Right to Information Act was passed in 2005.
(D) The Press Council of India can send journalists to prison for unethical reporting.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D)
Why: (D) is not correct. The Press Council can warn, admonish or censure a newspaper or journalist. It cannot impose prison terms.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (C) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: The Constitution does not name the press separately; its freedom comes from Article 19(1)(a).

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question: Which body measures television audiences and produces ratings in India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) BARC India
Why: The Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC) India measures viewership and publishes ratings.
Why not the others: (A) regulates telecom and broadcasting carriage. (B) is the public broadcaster. (D) oversees the press.
Key point: Ratings guide programming and advertising.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question: The Lumière brothers' machine, which worked as camera, printer and projector, was called the ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Cinématographe
Why: The Cinématographe could record, print and project film, and was used at their 1895 show.
Why not the others: (A) was Edison's peep-show viewer. (C) and (D) are other early devices.
Key point: Projection let many people watch a film together.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: One region shown only as comic servants
questions.question: A TV serial repeatedly shows people from one region only as comic servants. This is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Stereotyping
Why: Stereotyping is a fixed, oversimplified image of a group repeated until it seems natural.
Why not the others: (B) is the media deciding which issues seem important. (C) is selecting what gets published. (D) is the spread of cultural traits between societies.
Key point: Representation in the media shapes how groups are seen.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question: A journalist's ability to sense a story where others see nothing unusual is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A nose for news
Why: A nose for news is the instinct for spotting what is newsworthy.
Why not the others: (B) is fairness in reporting. (C) is understanding others' feelings. (D) is skill with words.
Key point: Inquisitiveness and a nose for news go together.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: A teacher discussing a lesson with a class of forty students is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Group communication
Why: A teacher with a class is one person communicating with a defined group whose members can respond.
Why not the others: (A) is communication with oneself. (C) reaches large, scattered audiences through media. (D) usually means two people.
Key point: The levels are intrapersonal, interpersonal, group and mass.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

Asha, a trainee reporter at a district daily, files this draft late one evening:

"The monsoon has always been a mixed blessing for the people of the valley. Farmers wait for it eagerly, and children love the first rains. This year, however, things were different. On Tuesday night, after six hours of continuous rain, the Kosra river burst its banks near Rampur village. About 400 families were moved by the district administration to relief camps in the government school. No deaths have been reported. Officials said the water level was falling by Wednesday morning."

The news editor sends it back. "The real news is buried in your fourth sentence," she says. "Open with it, answer the key questions in the first paragraph, and arrange the rest in order of importance, so that we can cut from the bottom if space runs short. Then give me a headline, and a few lines to go under Rakesh's photograph of a family wading through the water with their goats." She adds a warning: "And do not use that video of a 'collapsing bridge' going round on WhatsApp. Nobody has checked where it came from."

Question: Which structure of news writing is the editor asking Asha to follow?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Inverted pyramid
Why: The editor wants the most important facts first and the rest in descending order of importance, so the story can be cut from the bottom. This is the inverted pyramid.
Why not the others: (A) tells events in the order they happened, which is what Asha's draft does. (B) keeps the main point for the end. (D) mixes a news top with a narrative ending.
Key point: The inverted pyramid lets a reader get the news from the first paragraph.

Question: The first paragraph of a news story, which the editor wants to answer the key questions, is called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Lead
Why: The lead (or intro) is the opening paragraph that gives the most important facts of the story.
Why not the others: (A) is the line naming the reporter. (B) gives the place and date of filing. (C) is a short line set above a headline.
Key point: A good lead answers most of the 5Ws and 1H.

questions.sub_topic: Which of the 5Ws and 1H a phrase answers
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

Asha, a trainee reporter at a district daily, files this draft late one evening:

"The monsoon has always been a mixed blessing for the people of the valley. Farmers wait for it eagerly, and children love the first rains. This year, however, things were different. On Tuesday night, after six hours of continuous rain, the Kosra river burst its banks near Rampur village. The news editor sends it back. "The real news is buried in your fourth sentence," she says. She adds a warning: "And do not use that video of a 'collapsing bridge' going round on WhatsApp. Nobody has checked where it came from."

Question: In the draft, the phrase "after six hours of continuous rain" mainly answers which of the following questions?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Why?
Why: The phrase gives the cause of the flood, so it answers why the river burst its banks.
Why not the others: (A) is answered by the families and the administration. (B) is answered by "near Rampur village". (C) is answered by "on Tuesday night".
Key point: The 5Ws and 1H are who, what, when, where, why and how.

Question: The few lines the editor wants under Rakesh's photograph are called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Caption
Why: A caption (also called a cutline) is the text under a photograph that explains what it shows.
Why not the others: (A) sits above the story. (C) is a short promotional summary. (D) names the reporter.
Key point: A caption should identify the people, place and action in the photo.

questions.sub_topic: Why the WhatsApp video is rejected
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

Asha, a trainee reporter at a district daily, files this draft late one evening:

"The monsoon has always been a mixed blessing for the people of the valley. Farmers wait for it eagerly, and children love the first rains. This year, however, things were different. On Tuesday night, after six hours of continuous rain, the Kosra river burst its banks near Rampur village. About 400 families were moved by the district administration to relief camps in the government school. No deaths have been reported. Officials said the water level was falling by Wednesday morning."

The news editor sends it back. "The real news is buried in your fourth sentence," she says. "Open with it, answer the key questions in the first paragraph, and arrange the rest in order of importance, so that we can cut from the bottom if space runs short. Then give me a headline, and a few lines to go under Rakesh's photograph of a family wading through the water with their goats." She adds a warning: "And do not use that video of a 'collapsing bridge' going round on WhatsApp. Nobody has checked where it came from."

Question: Why is the editor right to refuse the WhatsApp video of the "collapsing bridge"?
options: A) Unchecked content may be fake news
B) Newspapers may not print any video
C) The video is protected by copyright only
D) The bridge lies outside the district
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Unchecked content may be fake news
Why: The source of the video has not been verified. Publishing it could spread fake news and damage the paper's credibility.
Why not the others: (B) is irrelevant, since the paper would only describe it. (C) is not the editor's reason. (D) is not stated in the case.
Key point: Verification before publication is a basic duty of a journalist.
